steps.name: GO Biological Process over-representation (with ranked fallback) on treated vs control DE genes
caveats: If fewer than ~50 genes pass padj<0.05, a hypergeometric ORA on that short list has essentially no power and result stability is poor under small threshold changes — the ranked gseGO fallback is used instead and this must be stated plainly in the output, not silently substituted
GO terms nest heavily; even after rrvgo reduction expect blocks of correlated/overlapping significant terms rather than fully independent findings
clusterProfiler's built-in GO annotation via org.Hs.eg.db/GO.db is the primary source; the MSigDB GOBP GMT reference is available as a cross-check but is not required if the OrgDb route succeeds
steps.context: Reference GO Biological Process gene sets for human are available at /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-go-human/2026.1/c5.go.bp.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt (7,538 GOBP_* sets, HGNC symbols) as a fallback/cross-check source if enrichGO's internal GO.db annotation needs supplementing; org.Hs.eg.db (v3.23.1) and GO.db (v3.23.1) are confirmed installed and are the primary route via clusterProfiler::enrichGO/gseGO.
steps.question: Which GO biological processes are over-represented among genes significant (padj<0.05) in the atopic dermatitis lesional vs control DESeq2 contrast, using the full set of 12000 tested genes as the statistical background?

grounding.reason: GO BP over-representation via enrichGO with tested-gene universe, rrvgo term reduction (R-0095), with the <50-significant-genes flag (R-0103) triggering the ranked gseGO fallback on the Wald statistic (R-0099) instead of an underpowered ORA.

constraints: universe must be the 12000 genes actually tested in the DESeq2 contrast, never the whole genome or whole annotation
apply the <50-significant-genes rule strictly: do not report an ORA p-value table built from a short gene list without triggering the ranked fallback
state the ranking metric (DESeq2 Wald stat) explicitly if the fallback path is used
gene set size window enforced at 15-500 members among tested genes
acceptance_criteria: Gene symbols from de_results.csv mapped to Entrez IDs via org.Hs.eg.db; the fraction of unmapped/multiply-mapped genes stated
Count of genes with padj<0.05 stated explicitly in the output
If significant gene count >=50: clusterProfiler::enrichGO run with ont='BP', universe = all 12000 tested genes (not whole genome), pAdjustMethod='BH', minGSSize=15, maxGSSize=500

If significant gene count <50: gseGO run instead on the full ranked list using the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat column) as the ranking metric, per fgsea/gseGO, with the same size window and BH adjustment; this choice and the underlying gene-count trigger reported in the output
rrvgo used to reduce redundant/nested significant GO BP terms to representative parent terms by semantic similarity (Wang measure), keeping the full unreduced table as a supplement
Output table includes GO ID, term description, gene ratio/NES as applicable, p-value, BH-adjusted p-value, and member/leading-edge genes per term
GO gene-set collection version and org.Hs.eg.db version recorded

plan.title: AD lesional vs control GO BP over-representation
plan.analytical_narrative: The DE results table (12000 genes tested, DESeq2 treated-vs-control contrast, atopic dermatitis lesional skin vs control skin, n=6/6) already exists, so no new differential expression run is needed. The research question is purely about GO biological process over-representation in the significant gene set. Before enrichment, sample-structure QC is run once to characterize the known caveat (sample_01 at ~4x below median library depth) so the downstream gene list is interpreted in that context — per DESeq2 best-practice, the low-depth sample is kept and reported, not silently dropped, since size factors already account for depth. The core enrichment step follows the grounded procedure: map DE result gene symbols to Entrez IDs via org.Hs.eg.db, count how many genes pass padj<0.05, and branch — if >=50 significant genes, run clusterProfiler::enrichGO (ontology=BP) with the universe restricted to all 12000 tested genes (not the whole genome) and rrvgo to collapse GO's redundant nested terms into representative processes; if <50 genes pass (per rule R-0103, a hypergeometric test on a short list has no power), run gseGO on the full ranked list (Wald statistic from the DESeq2 stat column) as the more powered fallback. Reference gene sets and organism annotation (MSigDB GO BP GMT, org.Hs.eg.db, GO.db, rrvgo) are all confirmed present in the environment. A final report step consolidates the enrichment table, the redundancy-reduced representative terms, the universe/database/version/ranking-metric disclosures, and the method-dependence caveat.
